context:
Tier-by-tier (w1 → w4) so user-visible value lands in priority order.
Tier 1 (percentile_ladder, cdf_chart) ships first because that's the
highest-impact gap for benchmark credibility.

Per-chart workflow (apply uniformly):
  1. Read the CLI implementation (find the textcharts call site,
     identify input shape and reduction).
  2. Decide where the math lives. Default: in
     `transformer.py`, emitted via the appropriate artifact
     (BenchmarkSummary for cross-platform; DetailResult for
     single-result). Avoid TS-side computation.
  3. Generate parity fixtures.
  4. Build the SVG component using `chartTheme.ts` constants and
     `useElementSize` for responsiveness.
  5. Wire into the appropriate page (Compare, ResultDetail,
     BenchmarkIndex, PlatformIndex).
  6. Vitest unit + parity test.
  7. Manual smoke at 3 viewport widths.

This item is sequenced AFTER the foundational items
(`explorer-establish-cli-explorer-parity-tests`,
`explorer-emit-comparison-artifact-from-pipeline`,
`explorer-unify-visualization-foundations`) because each new chart
needs the parity fixtures, theme constants, and pipeline-emitted
data structures those items deliver.
description:
The 2026-04-15 review found that the CLI registers **16 canonical
chart types** in `benchbox/core/visualization/chart_types.py:17-45`,
but the explorer implements only **6 visualization components**
(QueryHeatmap, QueryTimingChart, GroupedQueryChart,
NormalizedSpeedupChart, DivergingBarChart, MetaLeaderboard) -
and only 3-4 of those have CLI counterparts that compute the same
values. **10 CLI chart types have no explorer equivalent.**

Missing chart types and their importance for benchmark credibility:

  | Chart                | Why it matters                                                   |
  |----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | `percentile_ladder`  | Tail-latency P50/P90/P95/P99 - central to fair benchmark claims  |
  | `cdf_chart`          | Distribution shape - exposes "fast median, slow tail" patterns   |
  | `rank_table`         | Compact per-query ranking - denser than heatmap for many queries |
  | `distribution_box`   | Box-plot of per-query latencies - shows variance/outliers        |
  | `query_histogram`    | Per-query latency distribution                                   |
  | `time_series`        | Trend over runs - regression detection                           |
  | `cost_scatter`       | Cost vs performance - central to cloud-warehouse comparisons     |
  | `power_bar`          | Dedicated TPC Power@Size visual                                  |
  | `sparkline_table`    | Compact metrics summary with embedded micro-charts               |
  | `stacked_phase`      | Phase breakdown (load/warmup/power/throughput)                   |

This item ports each missing chart type to the explorer in priority
order. Every new chart consumes pipeline-emitted data
(per `explorer-emit-comparison-artifact-from-pipeline` - extending
the artifact emission as needed) and ships with a parity fixture
(per `explorer-establish-cli-explorer-parity-tests`) so the math
is verified against the canonical Python implementation from day one.

Out of scope: building entirely NEW chart types that don't exist in
the CLI either. Those should be evaluated and added to both sides
through the canonical chart_types.py registry first.

anti_patterns.dont: add a new chart in the explorer without a corresponding entry in chart_types.py
anti_patterns.instead: extend the registry first if a new type is genuinely warranted
anti_patterns.why: that recreates the divergence we're trying to eliminate

anti_patterns.instead: read the CLI's exact percentile method and either match it in TS or pre-compute in Python and ship in artifact
anti_patterns.why: Python's numpy.percentile uses linear interpolation by default and the numbers will differ

anti_patterns.dont: render cost_scatter when cost_usd is null for all results
anti_patterns.instead: hide the section entirely with a small note about cost data availability
anti_patterns.why: an empty scatter plot looks broken

anti_patterns.dont: replace the existing QueryHeatmap with rank_table on TPC-DS just because the heatmap is wide
anti_patterns.instead: add rank_table as an alternate view, let users switch
anti_patterns.why: users have built mental models around the heatmap

anti_patterns.dont: reuse PALETTE colors for time_series lines without a contrast check
anti_patterns.instead: extend chartTheme.ts with a dedicated TIME_SERIES_PALETTE if the 4-color palette is insufficient
anti_patterns.why: 4 line colors must be distinguishable when overlapping

anti_patterns.dont: skip parity fixtures for 'simple' charts like rank_table
anti_patterns.why: rank ties are exactly the kind of edge case where Python and JS sort algorithms can differ silently

preserves.behavior: BenchmarkSummary and DetailResult artifact backward compatibility - extensions add new fields, do not rename or remove existing ones
CLI chart_types.py registry as the single canonical source - explorer mirrors it, never the other way around
Existing 6 explorer chart components must continue to work - new charts add tabs/sections, do not replace existing visualizations
ResultDetail / BenchmarkIndex / PlatformIndex existing layouts and navigation patterns - additions are introduced as tabs or new sections, not page rewrites
